title: The complete phase diagram of detailed-balanced Gibbs samplers for the mean-field Heisenberg model
authors: Levente Raikovich, József Mák, Csaba Czabán, András Gilyén
abstract: We study the spectral gap of recently discovered families of KMS-detailed-balanced Gibbs-sampler Lindbladians for the mean-field Heisenberg model on $n$ spins. We show that the spectral gaps of these natural families of Lindbladians admit the same phase diagram: the gap is constant above the critical temperature (i.e., in the disordered phase), scales as $1/\sqrt{n}$ at the critical temperature, and as $1/n$ below the critical temperature (i.e., in the ordered phase). Our result builds on and extends the recent work of Basso et al.~(2026) which characterized this phase diagram for the GNS-detailed-balanced Davies generator, but only partially resolved the gap scaling at the critical temperature.
summary: This paper determines the universal phase diagram for the spectral gap of multiple detailed-balanced Gibbs samplers applied to the mean-field Heisenberg model. The key finding is that the gap scales predictably—constant, $1/\sqrt{n}$, or $1/n$—depending on whether the system is in the disordered, critical, or ordered phase, respectively. This provides deep insight into the convergence rates of quantum thermalization dynamics.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the universal phase diagram governing the spectral gap of various KMS-detailed-balanced Gibbs-sampler Lindbladians for the mean-field Heisenberg model.
main_result: The spectral gap exhibits a universal phase diagram: constant above the critical temperature, scaling as $1/\sqrt{n}$ at the critical temperature, and scaling as $1/n$ below it.
method: The analysis employs advanced techniques involving the spectral gap calculation via Dirichlet forms, symmetry decomposition (e.g., $R_n, P_n$), and comparing multiple generator constructions ($L_D, L_C, L_{F,\sigma}$).
model_or_system: The system is the mean-field Heisenberg model on $n$ spins, governed by the Hamiltonian $H_n$. The dynamics are described by Lindbladians ($L[\cdot]$) constructed to be KMS detailed-balanced, aiming to approach the Gibbs state $ho_{n, eta}$.
key_observables: The spectral gap ($\gamma(L)$) of the Lindbladians, which quantifies the rate of convergence to the equilibrium state.
important_parameters: Inverse temperature $ eta$, system size $n$, and the critical temperature regime ($ eta=2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on the KMS detailed-balance property and the ability to relate the gaps across different generator constructions via symmetry arguments.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first defining the problem across multiple Lindbladians, then using symmetry algebras to decompose the gap analysis, and finally establishing the universal scaling laws across different temperature regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, quantitative results on the convergence rates of quantum dynamics simulations (Gibbs sampling) for a fundamental model, directly impacting how one analyzes thermalization in many-body systems.
